title: AI Invoice & PDF Extraction
summary: A hybrid OCR and LLM pipeline that extracts structured information from invoice PDFs, using Surya OCR with a local Qwen2.5 model and an OpenAI API fallback.
overview: A document-intelligence pipeline that turns unstructured invoice PDFs into structured data and classifies invoices. It combines Surya OCR for text recognition with a local Qwen2.5 model for language understanding, and falls back to the cloud-based OpenAI API when needed.
problem: Invoices arrive as PDFs with varying layouts, so the information inside them is unstructured. Downstream finance workflows need that information as structured fields and a classification, which plain text extraction alone does not provide.
approach: Built a hybrid OCR and LLM pipeline to extract structured information from invoice PDFs.
Integrated Surya OCR with a local Qwen2.5 model and a cloud-based OpenAI API fallback for document processing.
Implemented fallback logic between local and cloud LLMs to balance processing cost, latency, and extraction quality.
Designed the workflow to support structured data extraction and invoice classification from unstructured documents.

architecture.label: OCR layer
architecture.detail: Surya OCR reads the invoice PDF.

architecture.label: Local LLM
architecture.detail: Qwen2.5 runs locally for extraction and classification.

architecture.label: Cloud fallback
architecture.detail: OpenAI API is used as a fallback to local processing.

architecture.label: Fallback policy
architecture.detail: Fallback logic balances cost, latency and extraction quality. The exact trigger conditions are not specified in the source material.

architecture.label: Why hybrid
architecture.detail: In general, a local model keeps routine work cheap and data on-premises, while a cloud model can serve as a higher-capability safety net. This is general architectural reasoning, not a verified account of the reasons for this system.

workflow.step: An invoice PDF enters the pipeline.
The local Qwen2.5 model extracts structured fields and classifies the invoice.
If local processing is not sufficient, the OpenAI API fallback is used.
Structured output is produced for downstream use. Output schema and validation rules are not specified.

items: Developed the hybrid OCR and LLM-based invoice classification pipeline.
Integrated Surya OCR with local Qwen2.5 and the OpenAI API fallback.
Resolved production dependency conflicts within the document processing pipeline to stabilize system behavior.
